## AI Competitive Analysis with Figranium

### How it works

This workflow starts from a form submission, then extracts structured data for both the user’s business and a competitor using Figranium. It splits and combines both data streams, aggregates the comparison inputs, and sends them to an OpenAI-powered LLM chain for competitive analysis. The generated analysis is then written into a new Google Docs document and updated with the final content.

### Setup steps

- Configure the form trigger with the fields needed to collect the user's business details and competitor information.
- Add and authorize Figranium credentials, and verify both extraction nodes target the correct submitted form fields or URLs.
- Configure OpenAI credentials for the chat model used by the Basic LLM Chain.
- Authorize Google Docs credentials and ensure the account has permission to create and update documents.
- Review the LLM chain prompt and the Google Docs document settings so the generated analysis is formatted as intended.

### Customization

You can customize the Figranium extraction targets, the aggregation fields, the LLM prompt for different competitive analysis frameworks, and the Google Docs document title or formatting.

## Collect analysis request

Starts the workflow when a user submits the form containing the business and competitor inputs.

## Extract and split data

Runs two parallel Figranium extraction paths: one for competitor data and one for the user's own data, then splits each extracted dataset into usable items.

## Combine comparison inputs

Merges the two split data streams and aggregates them into a single payload ready for AI analysis.

## Generate AI analysis

Uses the aggregated data in an LLM chain, powered by the OpenAI chat model, to produce the competitive analysis content.

## Create analysis document

Creates a Google Docs document and updates it with the AI-generated competitive analysis.

# Figranium vs Skyvern

## Executive Summary

Figranium and Skyvern both provide browser workflow automation, visual workflow construction, and mechanisms to run automations in production. Their strategic emphasis differs substantially.

Figranium presents itself as an open-source browser automation control plane: a visual block editor combined with scheduling, proxy rotation, stealth features, JavaScript execution, and a REST API. Its strongest apparent advantage is flexibility and deployment-oriented control for technical users.

Skyvern presents itself as an AI-powered browser automation platform for automating work across websites, especially portal-based business processes. It strongly emphasizes vision-based automation, CAPTCHA and 2FA handling, enterprise security, data extraction, and operational use cases. Its strongest apparent advantage is the breadth of business-facing capabilities and explicit enterprise positioning.

They compete directly in visual browser automation, data extraction, testing, and workflow execution. Figranium differentiates through open-source packaging, arbitrary JavaScript, and a single-binary control plane. Skyvern differentiates through AI agents, resilience to UI changes, authentication support, enterprise plans, and business workflow messaging.

The most important competitive takeaway is that Figranium appears better positioned around developer control and self-directed deployment, while Skyvern appears better positioned around enterprise adoption and automating complex human portal work. Neither company’s superiority is established across all dimensions by the supplied research.

## Head-to-Head Overview

| Dimension | Figranium | Skyvern |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Core offering | Open-source browser automation control plane with visual block-based workflow editing | AI-powered browser workflow automation using agents and vision-based interaction |
| Primary audience | Not explicitly identified; messaging suggests technical users and developers | Developers, enterprise users, operations leaders, and teams replacing manual portal work |
| Positioning | “Build complex browser workflows visually”; open-source, API-driven, deployable workflows | “AI agents to automate workflows on any website”; human-like browser automation |
| Key value proposition | Visual construction plus arbitrary JavaScript, scheduling, proxies, stealth, and REST execution | Automate logins, form filling, extraction, and portal workflows without brittle selectors or ongoing refactoring |
| Pricing approach | No plans or prices identified; described as fully open-source | Free, Hobby at $29/month, Pro at $149/month, and custom Enterprise |
| Major capabilities | Visual blocks, variables, JavaScript, scheduling, proxy rotation, stealth, recording, extraction, QA, REST API | AI/vision automation, CAPTCHA, 2FA/TOTP, extraction, document processing, form filling, SDKs, webhooks, self-hosting |
| Integration strategy | Workflow and deployment ecosystem including n8n, Make, Activepieces, Pipedream, and hosting platforms | Broad automation and CRM ecosystem including Zapier, Make, Clay, n8n, Workato, and others |
| Primary use cases | Data extraction, QA/regression testing, lead enrichment, price/change monitoring | Portal automation, accounts payable, document processing, form filling, lead generation, testing, and enterprise operations |
| Go-to-market approach | Open-source and developer-oriented, with GitHub and deployment distribution | Product-led free entry combined with paid tiers, demos, enterprise sales, and compliance-oriented messaging |

## Positioning & Audience

### Direct positioning overlap

Both companies emphasize:

- Browser-native automation across websites.
- Visual or simplified workflow creation.
- Data extraction.
- QA and testing use cases.
- Integration with automation platforms such as n8n, Make, and Activepieces.
- Production execution rather than only browser recording or prototyping.

Both also present their products as alternatives to more brittle browser automation approaches, although Skyvern makes this message more explicit through claims about avoiding selectors and reducing maintenance.

### Key messaging differences

**Figranium emphasizes control and extensibility.**

Its messaging centers on:

- Open-source availability.
- A visual block-based editor.
- Arbitrary JavaScript in the browser context.
- Built-in scheduling, proxies, stealth, and recording.
- A full REST API.
- Deployment as a single binary.

This implies a platform for users who want to design, customize, operate, and integrate browser workflows directly.

**Skyvern emphasizes intelligent automation of business work.**

Its messaging centers on:

- AI agents operating on any website.
- Human-like automation of portals.
- Vision rather than brittle selectors.
- CAPTCHA and 2FA/TOTP handling.
- Enterprise security and compliance.
- Replacing manual invoice, form, and data-entry processes.

Skyvern therefore makes a more explicit case to operations teams and enterprise buyers, while Figranium’s supplied messaging is more technically oriented.

### Developer, business, and enterprise emphasis

- **Developer emphasis:** Stronger for Figranium based on its open-source positioning, REST API, JavaScript blocks, GitHub CTA, and deployment integrations.
- **Business and operations emphasis:** Stronger for Skyvern based on accounts payable, document processing, form filling, lead generation, vendor portals, and manual-work replacement messaging.
- **Enterprise emphasis:** Stronger for Skyvern. It explicitly offers an Enterprise plan, enterprise security messaging, compliance positioning, dedicated support references, and enterprise use-case language.
- **Technical audience for Skyvern:** Also significant. Its positioning includes developers and engineers, native Python and TypeScript SDKs, Docker self-hosting, MCP readiness, APIs, and event streaming.
- **Figranium’s business audience:** Not clearly established in the supplied research, although lead enrichment, price monitoring, and QA features suggest potential business applications.

## Product & Features

| Capability | Figranium | Skyvern | Assessment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Visual workflow construction | Strongly emphasized through a block-based editor | Identified through a visual builder and browser recording | Roughly comparable in concept; different implementation emphasis |
| Custom code execution | Strongly emphasized; arbitrary JavaScript blocks | Mentioned through blending LLM reasoning with executable code | Figranium has the clearer explicit custom-JavaScript proposition |
| AI/vision-based automation | Not identified in researched pages | Strongly emphasized through AI agents and vision-based interaction | Skyvern has a clear advantage in stated AI positioning |
| Selector/UI-change resilience | Not identified in researched pages | Strongly emphasized; claims workflows survive UI updates | Skyvern’s stated differentiation is stronger |
| Scheduling and orchestration | Strongly emphasized; built-in scheduling and API execution | Webhooks and event streaming identified; scheduling not specifically identified | Figranium has the clearer built-in scheduling proposition |
| Proxy and anti-detection features | Strongly emphasized; proxy rotation and stealth evasions | Proxy networks identified; anti-detection not specifically identified | Figranium emphasizes operational browser controls more directly |
| CAPTCHA handling | Not identified in researched pages | Strongly emphasized as native CAPTCHA support | Skyvern has a clear stated advantage |
| 2FA/TOTP handling | Not identified in researched pages | Strongly emphasized | Skyvern has a clear stated advantage |
| Data extraction | Identified | Strongly emphasized, including structured JSON/CSV output | Both address extraction; Skyvern makes broader business claims |
| Document processing | Not identified in researched pages | Identified | Skyvern advantage based on available evidence |
| Variables and templating | Strongly emphasized | Not specifically identified in supplied feature list | Figranium advantage in explicit workflow data handling |
| Recording/captures | Identified | Browser recording identified | Both have the capability identified |
| REST/API access | Full REST API strongly emphasized | API integration and native SDKs identified; full REST scope not established | Figranium is clearer on a comprehensive REST control plane |
| SDKs | Not identified in researched pages | Python and TypeScript SDKs identified | Skyvern advantage in packaged developer libraries |
| Self-hosting/deployment | Open-source and single-binary deployment strongly emphasized; hosting integrations identified | Docker self-hosting identified | Both support deployment flexibility, with different packaging messages |
| QA and regression testing | Identified | Identified | Roughly equal based on supplied research |
| Enterprise security/compliance | Not identified in researched pages | Strongly emphasized | Skyvern has the clearer enterprise-readiness proposition |

### Most important product differences

1. **Automation method:** Skyvern’s central product claim is AI- and vision-based automation that can withstand website changes. Figranium’s central proposition is explicit, visual, programmable workflow construction. The research does not establish whether Figranium also supports comparable AI or vision capabilities.

2. **Authentication and interruption handling:** Skyvern explicitly highlights CAPTCHA and 2FA/TOTP support. These capabilities are not identified for Figranium in the researched pages.

3. **Technical control:** Figranium explicitly supports arbitrary JavaScript, variables, templating, REST operations, scheduling, proxy rotation, and stealth evasions. This gives it a clear control-plane and customization orientation.

4. **Enterprise workflow breadth:** Skyvern explicitly identifies accounts payable, document processing, forms, vendor portals, HR operations, and compliance-oriented workflows. Figranium identifies extraction, lead enrichment, price monitoring, and QA, but its supplied use-case coverage is narrower.

5. **Packaging:** Figranium’s “everything ships in one binary” and open-source positioning differ from Skyvern’s combination of cloud plans, enterprise sales, Docker self-hosting, SDKs, and AI platform capabilities.

## Pricing

### Free offerings

- **Figranium:** No pricing plans or prices were identified. The product is described as fully open-source, but the research does not establish the exact commercial structure, if any.
- **Skyvern:** Offers a Free plan at $0/month.

### Entry-level and paid tiers

- **Figranium:** No paid tiers were identified.
- **Skyvern:** Offers Hobby at $29/month and Pro at $149/month.

### Enterprise strategy

- **Figranium:** No enterprise pricing, sales motion, or enterprise package was identified in the supplied pages.
- **Skyvern:** Explicitly offers a custom Enterprise plan and promotes enterprise security, compliance, dedicated support, and large-scale operations.

### Pricing segmentation and go-to-market implications

Skyvern has a clearly segmented pricing structure spanning free users, side projects, production teams, and regulated or large-scale enterprise operations. This supports both product-led adoption and sales-led expansion.

Figranium’s open-source positioning may reduce initial adoption friction for technical users and organizations that prefer self-directed deployment. However, the research does not establish whether it offers hosted services, commercial support, or an enterprise monetization model.

It is not possible to conclude which product offers better value because Figranium’s commercial terms and operating costs are not provided.

## Integrations & Ecosystem

### Figranium

Identified integrations and distribution channels include:

- n8n
- Make
- Activepieces
- Pipedream
- DigitalOcean Marketplace
- Hostinger
- Easypanel
- Glama

Figranium also emphasizes a full REST API, which supports integration at the control-plane level. Its hosting and marketplace references suggest a deployment-oriented ecosystem, particularly for technical users and self-hosted environments.

### Skyvern

Identified integrations include:

- Zapier
- Make
- Clay
- n8n
- Workato
- Freshsales
- Activepieces
- Pabbly Connect
- Phonely
- Integrately
- Eachlabs
- viaSocket

Skyvern additionally identifies:

- Python and TypeScript SDKs.
- Webhooks and event streaming.
- Docker self-hosting.
- MCP readiness.

### Competitive significance

Skyvern has the broader identified integration list and more explicit packaged developer interfaces through native SDKs and event-streaming capabilities. Its inclusion of Workato, Zapier, Clay, and CRM-related integrations also supports a stronger business-automation and enterprise ecosystem position.

Figranium’s ecosystem is smaller in the supplied research but aligns closely with open-source, low-code, self-hosted, and deployment workflows. Its full REST API and single-binary positioning may appeal to users who prioritize operational control over breadth of prebuilt connectors.

The evidence supports a difference in ecosystem strategy rather than a definitive conclusion about integration quality.

## Strengths & Weaknesses

### Figranium

**Strengths**

1. **Clear open-source and deployment proposition:** The product is described as fully open-source and packaged as a single binary.
2. **Strong workflow programmability:** Arbitrary JavaScript blocks, variables, templating, and data transformation support custom browser logic.
3. **Operational control features:** Built-in scheduling, proxy rotation, stealth evasions, captures, and recording are prominently identified.
4. **API-first execution model:** A full REST API is explicitly emphasized for running workflows and controlling operations.
5. **Technical distribution channels:** Integrations with n8n, Make, Activepieces, Pipedream, and hosting platforms support developer and self-hosted adoption.

**Weaknesses / Risks**

1. **Enterprise proposition is underdeveloped in the supplied research:** Enterprise security, compliance, dedicated support, and formal enterprise packaging were not identified.
2. **AI differentiation is not evident:** AI agents, vision-based interaction, and UI-change resilience are not identified in the researched Figranium pages.
3. **Authentication automation gap is possible:** CAPTCHA and 2FA/TOTP handling are not identified. This is a potential competitive disadvantage for complex portal workflows, although absence of evidence is not proof that the capabilities do not exist.
4. **Commercial model is unclear:** No pricing plans, hosted offering, support model, or enterprise pricing were identified.
5. **Use-case messaging appears narrower:** The supplied use cases emphasize extraction, enrichment, monitoring, and QA rather than broader operational processes such as accounts payable or document workflows.

### Skyvern

**Strengths**

1. **Strong, differentiated AI positioning:** Skyvern clearly emphasizes AI agents, vision-based interaction, and workflows that are claimed to survive UI updates.
2. **Broad business workflow coverage:** Its identified use cases include accounts payable, document processing, form filling, vendor portals, HR operations, extraction, and lead generation.
3. **Authentication and anti-interruption capabilities:** CAPTCHA and 2FA/TOTP support are prominently marketed.
4. **Clear enterprise strategy:** Skyvern offers a custom Enterprise plan and explicitly promotes enterprise-grade security and compliance.
5. **Broad adoption and integration path:** Free entry, paid tiers, SDKs, Docker self-hosting, webhooks, and numerous integrations support multiple buyer types.

**Weaknesses / Risks**

1. **Greater commercial and product complexity is possible:** The combination of AI agents, multiple plans, enterprise sales, SDKs, and broad workflow capabilities may require more evaluation and implementation than Figranium’s single-binary proposition. This is an inference, not an independently verified user experience.
2. **Dependence on AI-led positioning:** Skyvern’s differentiation relies heavily on claims about AI reasoning, vision, and resilience. The supplied research does not independently verify those claims.
3. **Less explicit low-level customization messaging:** Skyvern mentions executable code, but Figranium provides the clearer claim around arbitrary JavaScript in the browser context.
4. **Open-source positioning is not established:** Skyvern supports Docker self-hosting, but the supplied research does not describe it as fully open-source. This may matter to buyers prioritizing source availability and control.
5. **Enterprise pricing may limit accessibility:** The Enterprise tier is custom, and the Pro tier is $149/month, potentially creating a higher apparent commercial threshold for some users than an open-source alternative.

## Where Each Company Appears Stronger

### Where Figranium appears stronger

- **Open-source and self-directed deployment:** Figranium explicitly describes itself as fully open-source and ships in one binary.
- **Workflow-level programmability:** Its arbitrary JavaScript, variables, and templating provide a clearer customization proposition.
- **Browser execution controls:** Scheduling, proxy rotation, stealth evasions, and REST control are strongly emphasized.
- **Technical control-plane positioning:** The full REST API and deployment integrations make Figranium appear particularly suited to developers building or operating custom automation infrastructure.
- **Potential adoption accessibility for technical users:** Although pricing is unknown, open-source distribution and GitHub-oriented calls to action may reduce initial barriers for self-directed technical evaluation.

### Where Skyvern appears stronger

- **Enterprise positioning:** Skyvern has explicit enterprise pricing, security, compliance, and operational messaging.
- **AI and UI resilience:** Skyvern strongly emphasizes vision-based automation and workflows that survive UI updates; comparable Figranium capabilities were not identified.
- **Complex authentication workflows:** CAPTCHA and 2FA/TOTP handling are clearly marketed by Skyvern.
- **Business process breadth:** Accounts payable, document processing, vendor portals, HR operations, and form workflows broaden Skyvern’s business appeal.
- **Pricing clarity and buyer segmentation:** Free, Hobby, Pro, and Enterprise plans provide a clearer path from experimentation to production and enterprise procurement.

## Competitive Threats & Opportunities

### For Figranium

**Threats posed by Skyvern**

- Skyvern may attract organizations seeking a complete solution for portal automation rather than a programmable automation control plane.
- Its explicit CAPTCHA and 2FA/TOTP messaging addresses difficult workflow barriers that Figranium does not identify.
- Enterprise security, compliance, and dedicated support messaging may make Skyvern easier to evaluate for regulated or larger organizations.
- Skyvern’s AI and vision positioning may reduce perceived maintenance burden compared with manually designed workflows.
- Skyvern’s broader integrations and SDKs could improve adoption among business automation teams and developers.

**Opportunities for differentiation**

- Make the open-source model more concrete by clearly communicating deployment, hosting, support, and any commercial options.
- Strengthen the developer case around arbitrary JavaScript, REST control, variables, scheduling, and single-binary deployment.
- Demonstrate performance in use cases where deterministic execution and precise browser control matter more than AI abstraction.
- Clarify whether Figranium supports authentication, CAPTCHA, UI-change resilience, or complementary approaches to these problems.
- Expand or more prominently package use cases for technical buyers, such as API-driven extraction services, regression testing infrastructure, and monitoring systems.

### For Skyvern

**Threats posed by Figranium**

- Figranium’s fully open-source and single-binary proposition may appeal to developers and organizations that want greater deployment control or lower platform dependence.
- Arbitrary JavaScript and a full REST API may offer more direct customization for technically complex workflows.
- Figranium’s built-in scheduling, proxy rotation, and stealth features could be attractive for users prioritizing operational browser controls.
- Figranium may be simpler to deploy in self-hosted environments, although this is not established beyond its single-binary messaging and hosting integrations.

**Opportunities for differentiation**

- Make the technical extensibility story more explicit, particularly around custom JavaScript, deterministic execution, and integration with existing application stacks.
- Clearly explain the relationship between AI reasoning and executable, repeatable workflows to address concerns about predictability.
- Continue differentiating through verified enterprise capabilities, security, compliance, authentication handling, and support.
- Demonstrate measurable benefits of vision-based automation and resilience to UI changes, since these are central marketing claims.
- Clarify self-hosting, deployment, and data-control options for buyers comparing Skyvern with open-source alternatives.

## Strategic Recommendations

### Recommendations for Figranium

1. **Define the commercial and deployment model clearly.** Publish whether the open-source product is accompanied by hosted plans, commercial support, enterprise services, or other paid offerings.
2. **Target a sharper technical segment.** Build messaging and proof points around developers who need arbitrary JavaScript, REST-controlled workflows, scheduling, proxy rotation, and single-binary deployment.
3. **Address the enterprise trust gap.** Add clear information on security, access control, support, compliance, deployment governance, and operational reliability if those capabilities exist.
4. **Clarify the stance on AI and resilient automation.** Either introduce or explicitly differentiate against AI/vision-based approaches, especially around UI changes, CAPTCHA, and 2FA.
5. **Package technical use cases more visibly.** Turn data extraction, QA/regression testing, lead enrichment, and price monitoring into concrete workflow examples that show why Figranium’s control-oriented architecture matters.

### Recommendations for Skyvern

1. **Strengthen the developer-control narrative.** Make custom code, APIs, SDKs, deterministic execution, and self-hosting as prominent as the AI-agent message.
2. **Prove core AI claims with evidence.** Use benchmarks or detailed examples to substantiate claims about selector-free automation, UI-change resilience, and reduced maintenance.
3. **Differentiate the plans by operational outcomes.** Clearly connect Free, Hobby, Pro, and Enterprise tiers to workflow volume, support, security, deployment, or collaboration requirements.
4. **Address open-source and deployment comparisons.** Explain the practical benefits of Skyvern’s Docker self-hosting and how it compares with single-binary or open-source alternatives.
5. **Maintain enterprise differentiation while improving technical adoption.** Continue emphasizing compliance, authentication, and business workflows, but provide a low-friction technical path through SDK examples, APIs, and ready-to-run workflows.

## Key Takeaways

- Figranium is positioned as an open-source, programmable browser automation control plane; Skyvern is positioned as an AI agent platform for business and enterprise workflows.
- Figranium’s clearest advantages are arbitrary JavaScript, REST control, scheduling, proxy and stealth features, and single-binary deployment.
- Skyvern’s clearest advantages are AI/vision positioning, CAPTCHA and 2FA/TOTP handling, enterprise packaging, and broader business workflow coverage.
- Skyvern has the more developed pricing and enterprise go-to-market structure based on the supplied research.
- Figranium’s commercial model and enterprise readiness are not established in the researched pages, creating uncertainty for larger buyers.
- Skyvern’s AI and UI-resilience claims are central to its differentiation but are presented as marketing claims rather than independently verified results.
- The most important strategic choice for buyers is between Figranium’s control-oriented, open-source approach and Skyvern’s AI-led, enterprise-oriented automation model.
